content.overview: BNS s. 74 — Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty (old 354). The old 354 cluster is now a family: 74 modesty, 75 sexual harassment, 76 disrobe, 77 voyeurism, 78 stalking, 79 word/gesture.
In student language: BNS s. 74 is the rule on “Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty”. The section provides that whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 74 exists so that “Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
74. Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine

learningObjectives: Understand the offence of outraging a woman's modesty under BNS s. 74.
Analyze the essential elements: assault or criminal force, accompanied by intention or knowledge of outraging modesty.
Examine the statutory penalty: imprisonment of one to five years and fine.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 74 provides that whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A woman's modesty is an attribute of her feminine gender. Any physical assault or application of criminal force that violates female dignity, decencies of behavior, or bodily integrity with requisite criminal intent is penalized as a serious offence against the person.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 74 (corresponding to IPC s. 354).
Actus reus: Assault (s. 130) or Criminal force (s. 129).
Victim: Any woman (of any age, including infant or sleeping woman).
Mens rea: Intending to outrage, OR knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty.
Penalty: Imprisonment not less than one year, extending up to five years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused assaulted her or used criminal force against her.
The accused did so with the intention of outraging her modesty, OR with knowledge that it was likely to outrage her modesty.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 74 protects women from non-consensual physical indignity that falls short of rape. 'Modesty' is not defined in the statute, but judicial precedent defines it as the reserve, dignity, and bodily sanctity inherent to female personhood. It belongs to all women regardless of age, marital status, or character; a seven-month-old female infant or an unconscious patient possesses modesty in law. The test is objective: would the act shock the sense of decency of a reasonable person? Touching a woman inappropriately in a public bus, grabbing her clothing, or forcibly embracing her satisfies s. 74.
examples: Teaching example (Inappropriate touch in crowd): An accused on a crowded bus intentionally grabs a woman's breast. This constitutes criminal force with intent to outrage modesty; s. 74 applies.
Teaching example (Pulling clothing): An employer angrily grabs a female employee's scarf and pulls it forcefully in an office dispute. This use of criminal force outrages her modesty under s. 74.
distinctions: Section 74 (Physical assault) vs Section 79 (Verbal/gesture insult): Section 74 requires physical assault or criminal force; Section 79 covers spoken words, sounds, gestures, or exhibition of objects without physical touch.
Section 74 vs Section 76 (Disrobing): Section 74 is general outraging of modesty (1 to 5 years); Section 76 specifically targets intent to disrobe or strip the woman naked (3 to 7 years).
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who cornered a female colleague in an elevator and forcibly hugged her against her protests is liable under BNS s. 74.
Rule: Section 74 penalizes the use of criminal force with intent or knowledge of outraging a woman's modesty.
Application: Forcibly hugging constitutes criminal force, and doing so against her protests demonstrates knowledge that it would outrage her modesty.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under s. 74 and faces one to five years imprisonment.

shortAnswer: State BNS s. 74 rule on outraging modesty.
State the twin elements: assault/criminal force + intent/knowledge to outrage modesty.
